clue.text: Questions trivial reading matter concealed by bed cover

definitions.note: a set of exam questions, taken as a single document

indicators.note: something concealed by a cover sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed
pap is worthless, undemanding reading material

explanation.surface: Someone hides light reading under the canopy of their bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed cover' suggests a quilt, but here it is the canopy over an old four-poster bed; 'concealed by' puts the trivial reading inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination script is the printed set of questions candidates must answer.

clue.text: Weapon taken from an aggressive man pursuing a cat

indicators.note: one who pursues comes behind, so these pieces follow the cat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
an gives the single letter A
a hawk is a warlike person, especially in politics

explanation.surface: A weapon is snatched from a belligerent man chasing a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used as a weapon by Native Americans.

clue.text: Star is laid up chamber

indicators.note: in a down clue, laid up means written upwards, so the run reads backwards

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A celebrity is confined to their room, ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' reverses SUN IS, the whole run read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a cavity in the skull bones, a hollow recess.

clue.text: Perennial favourite in examination not having succeeded

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
not having means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: a perusal is a careful examination of a text
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A lasting teacher's pet failed the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' drops the S from the examination word, leaving PERUAL; 'in' then puts the favourite inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something lasting or recurring endlessly.

clue.text: German coin and Chinese one, new, in typical money box?

indicators.note: these pieces sit inside the money box

parts.note: the classic children's money box is a piggy bank, shaped like a pig
the fen is a Chinese coin, a hundredth of a yuan

explanation.surface: Foreign coins of two nations sit in a child's savings box.
explanation.definitionFit: The pfennig was the small German coin, a hundredth of a mark.

clue.text: Put down agent on vessel

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
re means on or concerning
SS, steamship, is a vessel

explanation.surface: An operative is placed aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash a revolt is to subdue or crush it.

clue.text: Portuguese province where Chairman receives bill

indicators.note: one who receives something takes it in, so the bill goes inside the chairman

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese Communist leader
CA is short for current account, the running bill one settles

explanation.surface: The province in which the Chinese leader is handed an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: Macao was a Portuguese territory on the south China coast until 1999.
explanation.definitionFit: The territory was governed by Lisbon as an overseas province before its return to China.

clue.text: Island not about to become, smaller

indicators.note: not means the following piece is left out

parts.note: Minorca is a Balearic island
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: An island that is not about to shrink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes CA from MINORCA; 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor means lesser in size or importance.

clue.text: Little dog in a state in Mexico

definitions.meaning: a tiny toy breed of dog

explanation.definitionFit: The tiny dog breed takes its name from the northern Mexican state.

clue.text: Light meal, some lettuce sandwiches

indicators.note: the words sandwich the run, which is held within them

explanation.surface: A snack in which lettuce is put between slices of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' says the words hold the run between them; 'some' is part of the text.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a simple dish of beaten eggs, a quick snack.

clue.text: Chap joins soldiers in house

parts.note: a chap is a man
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A man signs up with the troops billeted in a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country residence, the main dwelling of an estate.

clue.text: Former writing materials I have found to be costly

parts.note: ex- means former
pens are tools for writing
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone finds that their old stationery was dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean high in price.

clue.text: Was no longer a popular person

definitions.meaning: the past tense phrase meaning existed at an earlier time
a faded celebrity whose fame is over

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a verb form for past existence and the noun for someone whose day of fame is gone.

clue.text: True, one can go astray during journey

indicators.note: letters that go astray wander out of place, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loyal person may still lose their way while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can go astray' rearranges TRUE and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase means along the way, while travelling.

clue.text: Was plug in right that cracked on 30th April?

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the plug in the right socket broke at the end of April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges WAS PLUG IN RIGHT. The question mark marks the definition as an example: the witches' festival falls on the eve of 1 May.
explanation.definitionFit: The German witches' sabbath is held on the night before May Day.

clue.text: Hit difficulty — needed illumination

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit
a plight is a predicament

explanation.surface: Someone hits trouble and needs a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is the glow given off by lamps.

clue.text: Lacking information overnight

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means uninformed and also literally during the hours without light.

clue.text: Reduced to essentials, Kent lost disastrously

indicators.note: something done disastrously is wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: as printed these words give a T where the anagram needs a second E: the setter meant Kent lose

explanation.surface: The county cricket team lost badly and is down to its bare bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrously' rearranges KENT LOSE; as printed, 'lost' gives a T where the anagram needs an E. Kent is an English county with a cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton staff or service is the minimum needed, cut to the bare essentials.

clue.text: I could possibly hold every king and knave — I don't care about you

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so the middle pieces go inside

parts.note: I could possibly means I might
every means all
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king
the knave in a pack of cards is the jack

explanation.surface: A card player wonders if they might have every king and jack, caring nothing for others.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a British catchphrase for selfish complacency.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase expresses smug indifference to other people's troubles once one is comfortable oneself.

clue.text: Such an inhuman way to ensure work gets done

definitions.text: Such an inhuman way to ensure work gets done

parts.words: Such an inhuman way to ensure work gets done
parts.note: a mechanical manner of working, like a machine that does labour without feeling

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a mechanical, emotionless way of working, like an automated worker.

clue.text: Italian birds, number caged

indicators.note: a caged thing is held inside, so one piece goes within the birds

parts.note: geese are birds

explanation.surface: Birds from Italy are counted while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Genoese means from Genoa, the Italian port.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Genoa is an Italian.

clue.text: Usual traffic system in river is a huge success

indicators.note: the success is put in the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river
a wow is a sensational hit

explanation.surface: Normal flow of boats on the river is a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is the longest river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-way traffic runs in both directions, the normal arrangement on roads.

clue.text: Youngster in uniform seen to devour mostly sugar?

parts.note: to wolf food is to devour it

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a sugar cube; the question mark flags that sugar stands for one lump

explanation.surface: A uniformed child is caught gobbling up nearly all the sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: A wolf cub is a junior member of the Scout movement, who wore uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubs are the junior branch of the Scouts, children in uniform.

clue.text: Vaguely sound reason for making money abroad

indicators.note: the word is said and heard only roughly alike

parts.note: sense means reason or good judgement

explanation.surface: A half-reasonable justification for earning money overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaguely sound' marks a near homophone: SENSE and CENTS are not quite the same in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Cents are small coins in America and other foreign countries.

clue.text: Required one third of length to be cut from thread?

indicators.note: something cut from a piece is removed from it

parts.note: a needleful is the length of thread put on a needle at one time

indicators.note: length has six letters, so a third of it is its first two

explanation.surface: Someone needs a third of a measured piece snipped off some thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one third of' takes LE from 'length'; 'to be cut from' removes it from NEEDLEFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is an old-fashioned word for necessary.

clue.text: Light refreshments, about a pound

indicators.note: the food goes about, around, the pound

parts.note: food is refreshment
L, for libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Snacks costing roughly a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is a verb: to flood a stage is to light it fully, as with floodlights.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood a scene is to bathe it in light from powerful lamps.

clue.text: In a storm, get wet on a horse-drawn vehicle

indicators.note: a storm throws things into disorder, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Caught in bad weather, travellers are drenched on an open carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a storm' rearranges GET WET ON A.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagonette is a four-wheeled open carriage pulled by horses.

clue.text: Moving a short distance

definitions.meaning: active and astir, as in up and walking

explanation.definitionFit: The word means astir, as when a patient is up and walking, and also nearby, as in somewhere close at hand.

clue.text: Mythical creatures — still ones

parts.note: still means yet
I is the Roman numeral one, so two of them are Is

explanation.surface: Legendary beasts that are quiet and solitary.
explanation.definitionFit: Abominable snowmen are the legendary apes of the Himalaya.

clue.text: Registered for flight — or chickened out?

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger wonders whether they reported at the airport desk or lost their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chickened out' looks like one idiom, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on 'chickened'.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers report at the airline desk before boarding a plane.
